_comment: Body app, Train tab. Three routines (beginner on machines and cables, intermediate adds dumbbells, hardcore on free weights), a sprint session, the effort scale, the log format and the first-day walkthrough. Every routine fits 20 to 30 minutes including rest, counted at 45 seconds a set (90 for a-side moves and back-to-back pairs), the listed rest after every set, plus warm-up and cool-down. The key 'machine' holds any exercise, free weights included, because train.js and the reader's log key on it. book_stephen is kept as an empty stub; nothing reads it. Not medical advice.
principles: Hard has a signal: your reps slow down.
Slowing reps mean you're near your max.
Machines and cables are the easy way in. Free weights work too.

effort.name: Know what hard is
effort.how: Hard has a signal: your reps slow down. That's how you know you're near your max. After each set, count the clean reps you had left.

scale.feels: Easy. Every rep feels the same.
Working. The last rep starts to slow.
Hard. Your reps are clearly slowing.
Very hard. The last rep grinds.
All out. The weight stops moving.
scale.use: Cables, curls and raises. Never under a bar.

effort.rule: Top of the range with reps to spare? Add weight. Can't reach the bottom? Go lighter.

log.how: One line per exercise: settings, weight, reps, what was left.

setup_basics.how: Line the handles or pads up with the muscle doing the work.
Match the colored dot to the joint that moves.
Snug the pads. Start with a stretch. Nothing should pinch.
Do eight easy reps, then adjust.
One second out, two seconds back. Don't let the stack slam.
Out on the push, in on the return.

routines.name: Beginner
routines.who: New, or back after a long break. Machines and cables are the easy way in.
routines.schedule: Any three days, with a rest day between.
routines.warmup: Three easy minutes on a bike or treadmill.
routines.progression: Hard means your reps start to slow. Get there every set. Hit 12 on both sets? Add weight.

exercises.setup: Back flat on the pad, feet shoulder width.
exercises.how: Push through your whole foot. Don't lock your knees. Lower slowly.

exercises.setup: Handles at mid chest, back on the pad.
exercises.how: Press until your arms are nearly straight. Return slowly.

exercises.setup: Thigh pad snug. Grip a little wider than your shoulders.
exercises.how: Pull the bar to your upper chest. Let it rise slowly.

exercises.setup: Cable station or row machine. Sit tall.
exercises.how: Pull to your stomach, elbows close. Reach forward slowly.

exercises.setup: Knee on the pivot dot, pad just above your heels.
exercises.how: Curl down and back, pause, return slowly.

routines.name: Intermediate
routines.who: Two months of steady training. Time to add dumbbells.
routines.schedule: Alternate Day A and Day B.
routines.warmup: Three easy minutes, then one light set of the first move.
routines.progression: Your reps should clearly slow by the end of every set. Hit the top of the range on all sets? Add weight.

exercises.setup: Feet shoulder width, knees over your toes.
exercises.how: Go deep while your lower back stays on the pad.

exercises.setup: Flat bench, dumbbells at your chest.
exercises.how: Press up. Lower slowly to a stretch.

exercises.setup: Seated, back supported, dumbbells at your shoulders.
Rope on the high pulley, elbows at your sides.
exercises.how: Push down until your arms are straight. Control the way up.

exercises.setup: Thigh pad snug. Grip a little wider than your shoulders.
exercises.how: Pull to your upper chest. Slow on the way up.

exercises.setup: Cable station or row machine. Sit tall.
exercises.how: Pull to your stomach. Squeeze your shoulder blades.

exercises.setup: Dumbbells at your thighs, knees soft.
exercises.how: Push your hips back until your hamstrings pull. Keep your back flat. Stand tall.

exercises.setup: Low pulley, elbows at your sides.
exercises.how: Curl up. Lower all the way.

routines.name: Hardcore
routines.who: A year of steady training. You've moved past the machines.
routines.schedule: Push, Pull, Legs, rest, Upper, Lower, rest. Only three days? Run Push, Pull, Legs.
routines.warmup: Five minutes: easy cardio, then two light sets of the first lift.
routines.progression: Every set ends with the bar slowing down. Top of the range? Add weight. Every sixth week, halve the sets.

exercises.machine: Cable curl and pushdown, back to back

routines.notes: Under a bar, stop at one left and use a spotter or safety pins. Zero left is for cables, curls and raises.

sprints.name: Sprint session
sprints.why: Short, fast bursts build speed and conditioning.
sprints.days_per_week: Once or twice, away from heavy leg days
sprints.where: A track, a flat path or a gentle hill. Bike or rower when it's icy.

warmup.what: Leg swings, lunges and high knees

main.rest_how: Walk back slowly. Go when your breathing settles.
main.progression: Add a round a week, up to ten. Then go to 15 seconds.

sprints.log: Rounds, time and how it felt.
sprints.safety: Never skip the warm-up. Stop if anything pulls.

first_day.name: Your first day at the gym

steps.title: Get in the door
steps.how: Buy a day pass and find the machines. Nobody is watching you.

steps.title: Warm up
steps.how: Easy pace on a bike or treadmill.

steps.title: Learn one machine
steps.how: Start with the chest press. Set the seat, pick a light weight, do eight slow reps.

steps.title: Learn what hard is
steps.how: Add weight until your reps start to slow. That's near your max. Stop with three left.

steps.title: Run the circuit
steps.how: One set on each of the five beginner machines. Log each one.

steps.title: Book the next two
steps.how: Put two more sessions in your calendar.

first_day.after: Soreness for a day or two is normal. Go back within three days.
